hypotheses.G1: H_final beats P_final (program evolution, equal budget) on the AUDIT mean score: paired bootstrap CI of the difference (Bonferroni over 3 comparisons) has lower bound > 0.
hypotheses.G2: H_final beats A (one-shot synthesis) on AUDIT (same test).
hypotheses.G3_paradigm_transition: H_final beats H_initial (the best program after the initial round of the H arm) on AUDIT (same test) AND H_final implements a different hypothesis than H_initial AND the AST similarity of the two programs is < 0.6. This is the operational definition of a paradigm transition without human intervention.
hypotheses.descriptive: P_final - P_initial on AUDIT; best implementation of every hypothesis on AUDIT; per arm: number of code clusters (single linkage, AST similarity >= 0.6), mean pairwise AST similarity, mean pairwise behavioural distance on SELECTION; improvements of the best SELECTION score that happened after >= 2 consecutive non-improving steps (escapes from stagnation); synthesis cost.
hypotheses.attribution: Failure attribution labels are derived from measurements only: a hypothesis with no executable implementation is 'untested' (never 'refuted'); 'mechanism inferior' requires >= 2 independent implementations each significantly below the leader; with one implementation the label is 'idea and implementation not separated'. Causes named by the model are stored as conjectures.
hypotheses.statistics: paired bootstrap over audit instances; a claim is SUPPORTED only if it holds in every replicate, MIXED if in some, NOT SUPPORTED if in none.
hypotheses.leakage_controls: generator sees the public spec, format examples, public family descriptions, programs, and for DEV instances the input, its own output, score and checker message. SELECTION: aggregate use only (leader / champion choice). AUDIT: one evaluation at the end.
hypotheses.success_criterion: The method is said to beat the previous one in a domain iff G1 is SUPPORTED there; a paradigm transition is said to be demonstrated iff G3 is SUPPORTED there. Anything else is reported as negative or mixed.
